author: Karina Prieto
title: Leaders meet to discuss 'Moving Michigan Males Forward' - NewsBreak
text:
By Karina Prieto ,
5 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) – Michigan education, business, and state leaders met in Lansing Wednesday to discuss improving and strengthening education and workforce opportunities for men.
Governor Gretchen Whitmer signed an executive directive back in April, aiming to reach more Michigan men and get them connected with college and skills training. Those at the Lansing Center Wednesday are doing their part to “Move Michigan Males Forward.”
“The data is really staggering around gaps in male participation in colleges [and] in employment,” said Jason Wilson with the Michigan Dept. of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential.
Richard Reeves led the keynote discussion at Wednesday’s event. As the founding president of the American Institute for Boys and Men, he gave suggestions on how our communities can better support this demographic.
“It’s very gendered very early,” said Reeves. “So, I think kind of breaking that pattern through things like apprenticeships is a really good idea, especially as the more applied the learning, the more it skews more male.”
Reeves says certain education and policy changes can better prepare boys and men for the future, citing that through his research, he’s found “CTE, technical high schools, anything that’s more applied learning skews male.”
“A world of floundering men is not going to be a world of flourishing women, or vice versa, in case that needs to be added,” said Reeves. “The spirit here has to be ‘rise together,’ and if we don’t do it and we don’t use policy to signal and we don’t invest in our boys and men, we shouldn’t be surprised if we then lose them.”
Wilson says Wednesday’s turnout gives him hope for what MiLEAP will accomplish with the initiative in 2026.
“To see women leaning into this issue is very encouraging and very uplifting because this is going to need everybody,” said Wilson. “This is not something that men can do for men alone.”
Speakers at the event say a key part of seeing positive change in this area is emphasizing that moving men forward doesn’t mean that women and other groups need to move backwards. Reeves says we should remember it is not a ‘zero-sum’ battle.
